blocks.html:
Ranger

Role: Ranged DPS. Difficulty: Easy-Medium. Weapon: Bow (an off-hand "Guard" item appears in build examples).

DPSRangedBeginner friendly

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.bodyHtml:
Ranger is a kiting ranged DPS with a bow, easy to pick up, and a safe, strong choice for solo play and PvE damage.

Role and playstyle

  • Bow is the main weapon; build examples also show an off-hand "Guard" item alongside it aion2hub, date unknown1 aion2hub, date unknown2
  • Playstyle is "a mobile, kiting ranged DPS: lead with a high-damage Snipe, maintain pressure with Rapid Fire and arrow skills," using distance and repositioning to avoid melee entirely aion2hub, date unknown3
  • 47 total skills: 37 active, 10 passive (single source)

Difficulty

  • Rated Easy-Medium, "ideal for safe solo gameplay and mobile combat" and one of the more accessible damage options for new players Overgear, date unknown4
  • A separate source calls Ranger "a physical damage class that can kite and stay safe... a safe ranged damage option" for beginners timesaver, date unknown5

Confirmed across two independent sources: Ranger is friendlier for a new player than Assassin.

PvE and PvP standing

  • One source ranks Ranger as the second-best PvE class for clearing content, just behind Assassin, per early focus-group-test (FGT) player rankings aion2hub, date unknown6
  • A tier-list source says Ranger's sustained PvE output is stable, only slightly below Elementalist and Sorcerer leprestore, date unknown7
    • Flags that high ping causes intermittent skill release and reduced damage efficiency
    • Calls the class slightly squishy, needing good positioning
leprestore is a boosting/marketing tier-list site, lower trust, treat its ranking as directional. Exact rank is single-source/contested, but sources broadly agree Ranger is a strong, sustained-damage PvE pick.

A-tier PvP framing

  • "The cleanest roaming pick after Assassin," with range, traps, and mobility that let it dictate engagement terms ggwtb, date unknown8 kr-era

B-tier PvP framing

  • "A stable B-tier pick in the overall meta," from the same source cluster's search summary (date unknown)

Sources disagree on the exact tier letter but agree Ranger is a strong, safe, non-top-tier PvP pick behind Assassin for pure burst.

Party demand: Ranger sits in the "damage" role bucket (alongside Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, Assassin) rather than the guaranteed party-demand bucket (Templar, Cleric, Chanter), but is called "one of the safest overall picks with strong performance plus long-term role demand" ggwtb, date unknown9 kr-era.

Who should pick it: players who want a ranged, kiting playstyle with a lower execution barrier than Assassin, strong solo-leveling comfort, and reliable, if not chart-topping, group DPS, plus good survivability through positioning rather than raw defense.

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Level Byzel, Blessed Bow, and Gryphon's Arrow to 20 first; branch priority is Gale, then Snipe, then Rapid Fire.

Core kit

Named signature active skills across sources (naming varies by guide):

  • Deadshot, Snipe, Rapid Fire, Spiral Arrow, Griffon Arrow (also "Griffin Arrow")
  • Snare Shot, Drill Dart, Burst Arrow, Explosion Trap, Tempest Shot
  • Marking Shot/Marking Arrow, Suppressing Arrow, Gale Arrow, Arrow Scattershot
  • Silence Arrow, Arrow Rain, and Piercing Arrow aion2hub, date unknown1 pvpbank, date unknown2
Naming is inconsistent between sources ("Griffon Arrow" vs "Griffin Arrow," "Marking Shot" vs "Marking Arrow"), contested, likely the same skills under different transliterations. Also: aion2hub, date unknown3

Leveling order

  1. Bring to level 20 first (Season 3-era): Byzel, Blessed Bow, Gryphon's Arrow Vortex Gaming, date unknown4 kr-era
  2. Level 15 is sufficient: Supporting Fire, per the same source
  3. Branch priority (separate source): Gale for attack-speed buff uptime, Snipe for long-range opener amplification, Rapid Fire for consistent filler damage, with Aimed Shot progressing toward higher levels past 20 u4n, date unknown5

Rupture Arrow: re-prioritize

  • "The utility of Phantom Arrow and Rupture Arrow has significantly increased" in a recent balance pass, worth re-prioritizing Vortex Gaming, date unknown6 kr-era

Rupture Arrow: lower priority

  • Called out as lower priority since it is "less effective for total DPS" u4n, date unknown7

This directly contradicts across the two sources, likely a balance change between patches. Flag both and prefer whichever matches your live patch notes.

Ignore/deprioritize early: no source gave an explicit "never level this" list. The closest is the Rupture Arrow disagreement above, plus the general principle of committing to stated priority skills instead of spreading points evenly.
Passive priority: no reliable source found. None of the fetched Ranger guides named a specific passive-skill leveling order, unlike Assassin's Rear Smite/Assault Stance/Exploit Weakness order.
Mastery/chain skills: no reliable source found describing a Ranger-specific chain-system combo the way Assassin sources did. General chain-system notes come only from Assassin-focused sources and were not confirmed for Ranger.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap contested kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Push Snipe and Rapid Fire to skill level 20 first, lead passives with Focus Eye, and put the first Stigma point into Arrow Storm.

This build comes from Korean Inven and DCInside ranger-board threads, cross-checked against a KR top-player adoption tracker. Most steps below use the skill's own level (its 1-20 scale), not your character level, since only the level 23 Stigma slot is anchored to a character level.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Snipe (저격)Skill Lv 20core opener, unexpectedly strong even unspecializedInven, date unknown
2Alongside SnipeRapid Fire (속사)Skill Lv 20core filler, called highest total DPS by one sourceDCInside, date unknown
3Skill Lv 16 breakpointArrow Barrage, Pierce Arrow, Aimed Shotper Daevanion nodes ownedsecond priority wave at the lv16 breakpointDCInside, date unknown
4When points allowExplosion Trap (폭발의 덫)Skill Lv 8enough for the knockdown, deprioritize past thatDCInside, date unknown
5After core activesPassives (see below)see Passivesfixed order, confirmed across 4+ sourcesInven, date unknown

Order A: click-priority (recommended)

  • Snipe and Rapid Fire to skill Lv 20 first, named the top two to max by two or more independent threads Inven, date unknown1 DCInside, date unknown2
  • Then the Lv 16 breakpoint group (Arrow Barrage, Pierce Arrow, Aimed Shot) DCInside, date unknown3

Order B: single leveling report (contested)

  • Burst Arrow, then Piercing Arrow, then Gale Arrow, then damage passives, per one level-77 player's leveling report Inven, date unknown4
  • Conflicts with a separate thread calling Piercing Arrow a DPS decrease DCInside, date unknown5

Order A has more independent corroboration across separate Inven and DCInside threads and lines up with top-player adoption data. Order B is a single leveling diary that contradicts another thread on Piercing Arrow, so treat it as a data point, not the recommended path cielui, date unknown6.

Leave at level 1: dropped, no source named a specific Ranger skill to leave unleveled.

Passives

  1. First: Focus Eye (집중의 눈), raises accuracy and attack, recommended to skill Lv 30 or higher confirmed Inven, date unknown7 DCInside, date unknown8
  2. Then: Hunter's Resolve (사냥꾼의 결의), crit damage amplification, fill from spare armor passive sockets rather than dedicated points Inven, date unknown9 DCInside, date unknown10
  3. Then: Hunter's Spirit (사냥꾼의 혼), third in three of four sources, tied with Binding Eye in the fourth Inven, date unknown11 DCInside, date unknown12
  4. Later: Binding Eye (속박의 눈) or Concentrated Fire (집중포화), order between the two varies by source; Binding Eye is called essential since Snare Arrow and Arrow Barrage build hit count to proc it Inven, date unknown13
  5. Lowest: Close Range Shot (근접사격), lowest priority in every order found Inven, date unknown14

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Push both basics to skill Lv 20, lean on Snare Arrow and Explosive Trap for debuffs

    Whichever basic is already being spammed gets the first Specialization point around skill Lv 8.

    • Snipe and Rapid Fire are both reported unexpectedly strong even unspecialized Inven, date unknown15
    • Lean on Snare Arrow (올가미 화살) and Explosive Trap (폭발의 덫) for debuffs ahead of a Burst-Arrow-centered window, per one leveling report Inven, date unknown16
  2. Lv 12
    Daevanion board opens: prioritize Rapid Fire, Focus Eye, and Hunter's Resolve nodes

    Open Rapid Fire, Focus Eye, and Hunter's Resolve nodes first, then Combat Speed, then Cooldown Reduction Inven, date unknown17.

  3. Lv 23
    Stigma: Arrow Storm and Byzel's Authority to skill Lv 1 first

    Spend the first Stigma Shards on Arrow Storm (화살폭풍) to skill Lv 1 first, called highest priority for its damage coefficient DCInside, date unknown18.

    • Byzel's Authority (바이젤의 권능) to Lv 1 alongside it, swappable for Griffin Arrow Inven, date unknown19
    • Explosive Arrow (폭발화살) to skill Lv 5 next, for a large cooldown drop at that level Inven, date unknown20
    • Blessed Bow (축복의 활) to skill Lv 15, called close to mandatory for its party-wide crit-damage buff even at the cost of pulling every other Stigma back to level 1 FM코리아, date unknown21
  4. Lv 23-45
    Core kit online: rotate in the Lv 16 breakpoint group, then chain a full rotation

    Once Snipe and Rapid Fire hit skill Lv 20, rotate in the Lv 16 breakpoint group per whichever Daevanion nodes are already invested DCInside, date unknown22.

    • A level-45 player's reported cycle: Target Shot into Aimed Arrow into Ambush Kick into Griffin Arrow into Burst Arrow into Snare Arrow into Rupture Arrow, falling back to basic-shot spam once cooldowns desync Inven, date unknown23
  5. At cap
    What changes: hand off to the endgame Stigma and gear spread

    No reliable source found for Greater Stigma (level 45/50) picks specific to Ranger. See the Stigma picks and Daevanion board route cards below for the endgame spread once those slots open.

Gear while leveling

  • Weapon and Gauntlet Daevanion nodes are fixed on Combat Speed and Weapon Damage Amplification regardless of level band Inven, date unknown24 DCInside, date unknown25
  • Raise Accuracy and weapon-attack enhancement together while leveling to avoid ranged damage loss; positioning at optimal range takes priority over damage cycles cielui, date unknown26
  • One thread targets level 57+ gear with a level-67 bow as an early benchmark, treating 10 points of Power as roughly 1 percent attack Inven, date unknown27
  • Do not over-enhance early gear since it is replaced quickly; cap early enhancement at +1 or +2 and save deeper investment for gear kept longer mmoorpg, date unknown28
Gale Arrow has its own sub-debate: one thread argues skill Lv 16 is now sufficient since a balance pass reduced its relative efficiency, while an older source said Gale's utility had significantly increased in the same patch window Vortex Gaming, date unknown29 Vortex Gaming, date unknown30.
Avoid: over-enhancing early gear you will replace soon; cap it at +1 or +2 and save deeper investment for gear kept longer mmoorpg, date unknown31.

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Rangers get 5 Stigma slots from 13 total Stigma skills; PvE and PvP setups use different skills entirely.

Rangers have 11 active skills and 13 Stigma skills total, but can only slot 5 at once (single source for the exact numbers; video content itself could not be fetched directly, title/description only) YouTube, date unknown1.

  1. PvE stigma branches: Gale (attack-speed buff uptime), Snipe (long-range opener amplification), Rapid Fire (filler damage) u4n, date unknown2
  2. Season 3-era skill-level framing: push Byzel, Blessed Bow, and Gryphon's Arrow to level 20, keep Supporting Fire at 15 Vortex Gaming, date unknown3 kr-era
Contested/unclear whether "Byzel," "Blessed Bow," and "Gryphon's Arrow" are stigma skills or Daevanion-board active-skill nodes; the source's phrasing does not make this fully clear, so treat the mapping with caution.
u4n naming not corroborated: other sources (Ten Ton Hammer's Ranger stigma list, AOEAH's DPS build roundup, a Gameforge EU Ranger PvE/PvP thread) do not use u4n's Gale/Snipe/Rapid Fire terms, and the closest KR match found uses different names entirely (Bow of Blessing, Griffon Arrow, Power of Vaizel, Supporting Fire, see the level 45 set below). Treat u4n's framing as likely its own fan-name shorthand rather than a corroborated branch structure single source, unresolved naming mismatch.

PvE vs PvP split

Confirmed via two independent KR threads: PvE favors 축복의 칼날 (Blade of Blessing), 폭발하는 칼날 (Exploding Blade), 화살 폭풍 (Arrow Storm), and either 기습 차기 (Ambush Kick) or 바이드 (Void); PvP favors 기습 차기 plus stealth skills, and a "purity" (순수) stat/skill setup even for players who only dabble in PvP kr-era fmkorea, date unknown4 inven, date unknown5.

PvE means damage maximization, PvP means survival/ambush focus, per the stated framing.

Level 45 advanced stigma

  • Bow of Blessing (축복의 활): +7% Smite during its duration, stacks with a Chanter's party Smite buff, mandatory
  • Griffon Arrow (그리폰 화살): reportedly ~10% of total DPS share, also mandatory
  • Power of Vaizel (바이젤의 권능): 50% chance on crit to reduce all cooldowns by 1 second
  • Supporting Fire (지원 사격): flat attack power increase

Leveling priority is Bow of Blessing and Power of Vaizel first single source kr-era vortexgaming, date unknown6.

What to spend Stigma Shards on first: no reliable source found with an explicit "spend shards on X first" statement for Ranger, unlike Assassin, where multiple sources named Illusive Clone as the top shard priority. Closest guidance: the branch priority above (Gale, then Snipe, then Rapid Fire, inferred from listing order, not an explicit statement), or by leveling order for the level 45 set: Bow of Blessing and Power of Vaizel first.

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.headExtrasHtml: First board unlocks lvl 12 contested single source
blocks.bodyHtml:
Boards unlock every 10 levels from 12 to 45; put stat points into Smite first, then Critical Hit, then Attack.

Board unlocks

  • Nezekan (level 12), Zikel (level 20), Vaizel (level 30), Triniel (level 40), Ariel (level 45), Azphel (level 45) Fextralife, date unknown1
  • A separate search summary names eight total boards, adding Marchutan and Yustiel as additional level 45 advanced boards (date unknown)

Unclear if this is a page-version difference or a KR/TW-versus-global discrepancy, flagging both.

Node types

Class-agnostic, applies to Ranger the same as Assassin: grey = stat increase (1 point), green = passive skill level-up (2 points), blue = active skill level-up (3 points), orange/unique = special node (4 points) Fextralife, date unknown2. This matches the blue-active/green-passive framing used elsewhere in this guide (confirmed).

  1. Stat-node order (single source, no independent corroboration): Smite first, targeting 60%+ on helmet, cloak, and other key gear pieces
  2. Then Critical Hit, to maximize back-attack/critical damage output
  3. Then Attack and Attack Speed, to synergize with buff windows
  4. Then Accuracy, to avoid misses in endgame PvE, with HP and Defense as secondary, PvP-leaning priorities u4n, date unknown3
No Ranger-specific source directly compares blue active-skill nodes, green passive nodes, and stat nodes, or which to prioritize first; the closest is the stat-node order above. No reliable source found comparing active-skill-nodes-first versus stat-nodes-first for Ranger the way the Assassin Field Manual did for Assassin.
When to reset: no reliable source found for Ranger specifically.

Points sources: same general mechanism as Assassin, progression-based accumulation. No Ranger-specific farming guidance found beyond "you will eventually get enough Daevanion Points to cover the entirety of the boards" Fextralife, date unknown4.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Arcana is shared across classes; Rangers should lock in Rapid Shot, Snipe, Piercing Arrow, and Aimed Shot to level 20.

General system (class-agnostic)

Arcana cards grant Combat Power, skill bonuses, skill-level "transcendence" past normal caps, set effects, and stat amplification Vortex Gaming, date unknown1 kr-era expcarry, date unknown2.

General meta card-type mixes (not Ranger-specific): current meta trends toward 3 Vitality/2 Magic or 2 Vitality/3 Magic over the older 4 Vitality/1 Magic split. "Vigor 4 / Purity 4" is called one of the strongest long-term Arcana configurations currently available Vortex Gaming, date unknown3 kr-era.

Ranger-specific picks

  • Active-skill level-20 targets: 속사 (Rapid Shot), 저격 (Snipe), 송곳화살 (Piercing Arrow), 조준화살 (Aimed Shot)
  • Scales (천칭) card: pick one of five available skills, often Snipe, freeing that skill from another Arcana slot, plus a secondary option like "집중의 눈" (Eye of Focus/Focus stat)
  • If an evasion-stat build isn't feasible, a "공명치" (Resonance/HP-and-resist) stat setup is a fallback
  • Weapon and Guard Arcana slots should fix combat speed and weapon-damage amplification first, then flex the remainder toward power, accuracy, or multi-hit

single source kr-era inven, date unknown4 inven, date unknown5

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Bow is the only weapon; sources disagree whether DEX or Attack/Crit Damage should lead your stat priority.

Weapon: Bow (main-hand), with an off-hand item, "Guard," shown in one example build aion2hub, date unknown1.

DEX-first framing

  • Dexterity (DEX) named as the Ranger's primary stat, directly increasing attack accuracy, critical hit chance, and overall damage output, with Critical Hit and Accuracy called crucial for maximizing burst potential exitlag, date unknown2

Attack/Crit Damage-first framing

  • Attack Power and Crit Damage as primary, then Accuracy, then Attack Speed, then Crit Rate as secondary, then MP Recovery for sustained fights pvpbank, date unknown3
exitlag's page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, search-summary-derived, single source. Contested ordering between the two framings; both agree Accuracy and Critical stats matter early.
  1. Example PvE build (Level 45, Gear Score 4,902): a single community-submitted build using an Archon Praetorian Captain Bow + Guard (both +20 enchant, +5 exceed) and a full Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord armor/accessory set aion2hub, date unknown4

Pantheon selections: Destruction, Death, and Time, "for combat speed." Single community-submitted build, explicitly labeled by its creator as "an orientative test build, use it as a reference and tune to your gear."

Enhancement order

Same general cross-class order as Templar: weapon first for felt combat impact, then Guard, then accessories, with defensive armor pieces enhanced steadily mid-game.

  • Helmet: prioritize passive-skill options
  • Armor: prioritize damage amplification
  • Shoulders: prioritize critical damage amplification
  • Leggings: prioritize damage resistance

single source, Ranger-specific kr-era cielui, date unknown5

Set effects: "Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord" appears as the named armor/accessory set in the example build above, with stat contributions only, no explicit set-bonus text found (single source) aion2hub, date unknown6.

Manastone-equivalent priority: no reliable source found for a Ranger-specific manastone/socket enhancement order, unlike Assassin's Back Attack Boost, Weapon Damage Boost, Critical Damage Boost, Attack, Damage Boost ordering, which had a source.

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.bodyHtml:
Open with Griffin Arrow, apply Marking Arrow, then spam Piercing Arrow while repositioning constantly.

Beginner PvE rotation

Single source: pvpbank, date unknown1

  1. Open with Griffin Arrow, a straight-line, high-burst opener with a long cooldown
  2. Apply Marking Arrow, a debuff reducing enemy crit resistance and adding knockback
  3. Spam Piercing Arrow mixed with basic shots; it has MP-recovery/lifesteal specialization options for sustained damage
  4. Deploy Arrow Rain on cooldown, an AoE hitting up to six targets with a brief stun

PvP approach

Emphasizes burst-and-CC chaining: enter from Stealth, use Silence Arrow to shut down the opponent's actions, and use terrain/positioning control rather than a fixed combo string pvpbank, date unknown2.

Key playstyle principle: "Motion is your main defense." Rangers succeed through constant repositioning rather than tanking hits, requiring map awareness and cooldown management pvpbank, date unknown3.

A separate source echoes "keep moving to avoid being targeted" and warns damage windows are short, recommending Daevanion nodes to widen burst windows u4n, date unknown4.

Auto-hunt/macro setup is one of the better-documented areas for Ranger specifically. A YouTube guide title confirms it covers macro setup for skills, Stigmas, and the Daevanion board, though the video's actual content could not be retrieved, only YouTube's generic footer returned YouTube, date unknown5. A related written guide describes the macro setup as centered on four inputs (Left Click, Right Click, "3," "2"), and states developers have officially confirmed macros are permitted for aiming for high scores in dungeons, with Stigma skills also groupable into a macro via a "turbo" function Medium, date unknown6 (HTTP 403 on direct fetch, search-summary-derived only, single source, unverified in full).
Defensive/utility cooldowns: no reliable source found naming a specific Ranger defensive cooldown by name, unlike Assassin's Evasion Stance/Shadow Walk. Guidance is limited to the general "keep moving"/positioning principle above rather than a named skill.

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Ranger levels comfortably solo thanks to kiting, but high ping can break its skill timing.

Solo leveling comfort: Ranger is repeatedly described as comfortable and safe to solo-level, benefiting from ranged kiting and not needing to tank hits Overgear, date unknown1 timesaver, date unknown2. Confirmed across 2+ sources.

Sustain: MP Recovery is named as a secondary stat priority "for sustained fights," and Piercing Arrow has lifesteal/MP-recovery specialization options useful for extended pulls pvpbank, date unknown3.

Mob density/turn-on point: no reliable source found giving a specific level at which Ranger "turns on." The closest indirect signal is the stigma/skill guidance to hit Byzel, Blessed Bow, and Gryphon's Arrow at level 20, suggesting the core kit solidifies around that point, similar to Assassin's level 16-20 breakpoints. Inferred, not explicitly stated Vortex Gaming, date unknown4 kr-era.
Latency sensitivity: one tier-list-adjacent source specifically warns that high ping causes intermittent skill release and reduces damage efficiency for Ranger, worth flagging for a class that leans on precise skill weaving leprestore, date unknown5 (lower-trust marketing/tier-list site, single source).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Most Ranger mistakes come from standing still, poor cooldown timing, and skipping Accuracy investment.

  1. Standing still in combat instead of continuously repositioning ("motion is your main defense") pvpbank, date unknown1 u4n, date unknown2
  2. Poor cooldown management, letting short damage windows go unused u4n, date unknown3
  3. Suboptimal gear synergy, not aligning Daevanion nodes and gear stats to widen burst windows u4n, date unknown4
  4. Inadequate positioning in PvP specifically, getting caught out of range of escape tools u4n, date unknown5
  5. Ignoring Accuracy investment, leading to avoidable misses in endgame PvE content u4n, date unknown6
  6. Playing on high-latency connections without accounting for intermittent skill release, which reduces effective damage output leprestore, date unknown7 (single source, lower-trust)
  7. Chasing "meta" builds or perfect gear too early instead of leveling with the recommended core skill/stigma branches (Gale/Snipe/Rapid Fire)
Fewer Ranger-specific common-mistakes items exist than for Assassin. Items 1-5 above are directly sourced, item 6 is single-source, and item 7 is a general beginner-mistake pattern seen across AION 2 guides broadly, not Ranger-specific in its original source, applied here by extension and flagged as inference rather than a documented claim.
